lawyer:
Shamim Khaled Ahmed, Advocate instructed by Mr. Abu Siddique, Advocate-On-Record ------ For the Petitioners  
Mohammad Nazrul Islam, Senior Advocate instructed by Me Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, Advocate-On-Record ------ For the Respondent
parties:
Janata Bank, presently Janata Bank Ltd. Tanbazar Branch, S.M. Maleh Road, Tanbazar, Narayangonj and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
M/S. Haque Commercial Syndicate, Proprietor: Md. Nurul Haque Sarker, 20, Bangabandhu Road, Narayangonj ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 2. The facts of the case, in short, are that the respondent as plaintiff filed Money Suit No. 01 of 2006 before the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Narayangonj stating, inter alias that he is the proprietor of M/S Haque Commercial Syndicate, M/S Nurul Haque Textile Mills, M/S Nurul Haque, M/S Sylviatex Garments, M/S Sylvitex Packaging and M/S Sylvitex Dyeing and Finishing. He Maintained current account with the defendant No. 1 bank in the name of M/S. Haque Commercial Syndicate, M/S. Nurul Haque Textile Mills and M/S. Unitex Corporation and obtained Tk. 1,00,00,000/- (one crore), Tk. 25,00,000/- and Tk. 33,00,000/- respectively in total 1,58,00,000/- loan facility. Against the C.C. Pledge loan of Tk. 1,00,00,000/- in the name of M/S. Haque Commercial Syndicate, the plaintiff mortgaged 104.5 decimal land as described in 'Ka' schedule which is of worth Tk. 2,00,00,000/- after fulfilling all the conditions imposed by the defendant bank and thereafter the plaintiff was also continuing with his business as Per terms and conditions of the defendant petitioner bank. On November, 1990 the defendant No. 1 bank closed all the banking transactions with the plaintiff respondent and all the firms without giving any notice to him and also stopped delivery of pledged goods. On 17.11.90 total amount of pledged goods was 380 bales of cotton as per pledge card, stock chart, stock report, in and out report. The book value of the pledge goods were Taka 1,35,10,000/- and 25% margin of the plaintiff is Taka 33,77,500/- Day by day the pledged cotton is loosing its quality and also huge amount of interest is being imposed upon him. The plaintiff was the guarantor against the liability of the importer L/C of M/S. Md. Ashraf Ali (GL), M/S. Md. Jamaluddin (GL), M/S. Md. Somed Ali (GL) and M/S. Md. Ramzan Ali (GL). The defendant No. 1 bank verbally informed the plaintiff in January 1991 that a huge amount of cotton imported by the said importers had been lost from Benapole port against which the plaintiff was a guarantor. After 7 months, the defendant No. 1 bank delivered 151 bales of cotton on the request of the plaintiff against Tk. 39,12,000/- deposited in cash in the account of M/S. Haque Commercial Syndicate. The rest of the cotton was in the custody of the defendant bank having book value of 86,78,000/-. In the mean time the plaintiff paid Taka 50,00,000/- and Tk. 14,00,000/- in the account of M/S. Nurul Haque Textile Mills and Unitex corporation respectively as per the claim of the defendant No. 1 along With interest and obtained delivery of pledged goods. On 29.09.92 the plaintiff deposited Taka 39,12,000/- following the circular No. 2678 dated 31.01.92 of the defendant petitioner bank to get the waiver of interest which however the defendant petitioner bank did not sanction. Thereafter the defendant bank filed Artho Rin Suit Nos. 49 of 1992, 53 of 1992 and 54 of 1992 against the said 4 importers and the plaintiff. The plaintiff as the guarantor contested the suits by filling written statement and all those suits were dismissed by the learned Artho Rin Adalat, Narayangonj on 30.09.96. Thereafter the defendant bank filed First Appeal Nos. 473 of 96,474 of 96 and 478 of 1996 before the Hon'ble High court I Division against the judgments and decrees of the Artho Rin Adalat in the said four Artho Rin Suits. After hearing both the parties the Hon'ble High Court Division by the judgment and decree dated 20.11.2000 upheld the judgment and decree of the Artho Rin Adalat. In the judgment it was observed- "we also hold that the two cheques, one of Taka Ten lac and the other of Taka five lac were most illegally sent by the B.B. Road Branch to the Tanbazar Branch of the bank and were credited to the account of the imported in Mortgaged Suit No.54 of 1992 against the  instruction of the guarantor and the bank is obliged to return adjust taka fifteen lac of the aforesaid cheques against the dues of the guarantor himself in respect of his accounts as per his instruction." Thereafter the defendant bank filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal before the Hon'ble Appellate Division being C.P. Nos.735 of 2001, 736 of 2001, 737 of 2001 and 738 of 2001. After hearing both the parties the Hon'ble Appellate Division rejected all the petitions by a single judgment dated 04.08.2002. Though the plaintiff   on several occasions requested the defendant bank to waive interest to enable repayment of loan and to arrange delivery of the pledged cotton but the defendant petitioner bank did not respond to the prayer at all. On 19.12.1992 the defendant bank published an advertisement for auction sale of the pledged cotton in The Daily Ittefaq against which the plaintiff raised objection and as such the defendant bank proposed to the plaintiff to deposit Taka 3,00,000/- to stop the auction and to get the waiver of interest. The plaintiff on 27.12.1992 deposited taka 3,00,000/- and requested the defendant to stop the auction process and to waive the interest but the defendant bank continued with the auction process. The defendant No. 1 bank by a letter dated 04.04.1993 informed the plaintiff to repay Tk.67,55,090/- within 7 days to take delivery of the pledged cotton and also asked to follow schedule of repayment for the rest. Thereafter on 05.04.1993 in another letter the defendant bank asked the plaintiff to pay Taka 67,55,090/- within 7 days and the rest within 30 days. As the plaintiff failed to comply with the schedule, the cotton was sold by auction but the defendant bank could not deliver the cotton on 07.06.1993 due to discrepancy in the quantity of the cotton and returned Taka 67,50,090/- to the auction purchaser. The attempt to sell the cotton of the plaintiff was nothing but an illegal act. In this circumstance manager of defendant No.1 bank verbally proposed to the plaintiff to deposits some amount of money and apply for waiver of interest. In the mean time heavy rainfall caused flood which damaged the pledged cotton. In spite of such damage the plaintiff requested the defendant No. 1 on several occasion to waive the interest and deliver the goods but the defendant bank did not respond. On 11.05.94 the defendant bank informed the plaintiff to take possession of the vacant godown as the pledge goods had been sold for Taka 36,97,000/- but against that the plaintiff sent a legal notice on 07.06.94 through his Advocate to state the reason for sale by private negotiation but the reply being unsatisfactory, the plaintiffs learned Advocate sent second legal notice on 22.10.94 but received no reply. The defendant bank filed Artho Rin Suit No. 63 of 94 claiming Taka 78,70,728/- as on 31.10.94 which was contested by Md. Nurul Haque Sarkar by filing written statement who filed Writ petition No. 2020/98 against acceptance of additional statement filed by the bank. Moreover the defendant bank filed a criminal case on 31.10.94 in the Narayangonj police Station through the Bureau of Anti-Corruption to harass the plaintiff which is now pending before the Narayangonj Special Tribunal as Special Case No. 1 of 1998. As the defendant bank did not pay Taka 15,00,000/- pursuant to the observation in the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court Division as well as of Appellate Division, the plaintiff filed Misc. Case  Nos. 36 of 2002 and 40 of 2002 before the learned Artho Rin Adalat Narayangonj. On 29.08.2005 the learned court passed judgment in favour of the plaintiff with the observation to go to the proper court for getting the order for payment against the defendant bank. On the same self matter Money suit No 2 of 2003 was filed before the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Narayangonj and the suit was decreed in favour of the plaintiff on 27.11.2005 for Taka 1,50,82,000/- against the defendant bank along with 20% compensation and 20% trimonthly composition until payment. On these facts and circumstances plaintiff claimed total Taka 204,87,22,985.88.
